answer.reasoning: BBR and Westwood are least harmed by random non-congestion loss, while loss-based Reno/Vegas back off most aggressively at 0.1% loss.

At 1% random loss and 10ms RTT, loss-based AIMD flows are loss-limited, BBR is least sensitive to loss, Westwood recovers better with bandwidth estimation, Illinois/CUBIC outperform Reno, and Vegas backs off earliest under queue/loss signals.
With no random loss and ample buffers, most loss-based controllers fill the 100Mbit path, while BBR paces near bottleneck rate and Vegas backs off on delay before fully using the deep queue.
At 1% random loss with ample buffering, BBR is least loss-reactive, Westwood recovers better than classic loss-based controls, while Vegas backs off early and underfills the path.

With 0.1% random loss on an 80ms 100Mbit path, BBR is least loss-coupled, Westwood/Illinois recover better than standard AIMD, Reno/CUBIC are loss-limited, and Vegas backs off earliest behind the deep FIFO.
BBR largely ignores random non-congestion loss, Westwood recovers using bandwidth estimation, while loss-based AIMD variants are increasingly penalized by 1% loss and Vegas backs off earliest.
Vegas and BBR keep the standing queue smallest, while the loss-based algorithms fill the deep FIFO more aggressively, with Illinois and Cubic producing the worst latency under load.

Under a deep FIFO bottleneck, rr p99 is driven mainly by standing queue from the bulk flow: Vegas backs off on delay, BBR tends to cap inflight near BDP, Westwood is less aggressive after loss, while Illinois/CUBIC/Reno keep larger loss-driven queues.
With no random loss, low RTT, and ample buffering, all are near line rate; BBR/CUBIC fill fastest while Vegas is most conservative.
Vegas is delay-based and keeps the FIFO shallow, BBR limits standing queue better than loss-based controls, while more aggressive loss-based algorithms build larger queues under 1% loss.
At 0.1% random loss, BBR and Westwood maintain rate best, Illinois backs off less than classic loss-based controls, while Cubic/Reno/Vegas suffer frequent loss-induced cwnd cuts.
Vegas and BBR avoid persistent deep FIFO queues, while loss-based variants fill the 1000-packet buffer, with more aggressive growth generally causing worse rr p99 latency.

Vegas should keep the shallowest standing queue, BBR avoids loss-driven buffer filling better than Reno-family variants, while CUBIC/Illinois/Reno tend to saturate the deep FIFO under loss with CUBIC worst.
Vegas is delay-seeking and BBR is paced, while the loss-based variants tend to fill the 1000-packet FIFO, with more aggressive growth producing worse p99 queueing.
Delay-based Vegas should keep the FIFO shortest, BBR paces near BDP, while loss-based variants build larger standing queues with more aggressive growth causing worse rr p99.
